title: Commitment fitment suggestor and scaling simulator for dedicated fleets
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, tenant-aware suggestor that recommends a commitment profile (pool size + floor throughput) and validates it via a scalable simulator that replays realistic tenant demand patterns. The tool should help account teams and customers pick committed capacity that meets 99th-percentile throughput targets while minimizing monthly spend.

Scope:
- Ingest historical request traces and per-tenant P95/P99 latency and tokens-per-request distributions.
- Provide candidate configurations (pool shapes, min/target throughput, scaling policy knobs) ranked by expected cost and risk.
- A simulator that can replay traces with our autoscale policy implementations to surface potential SLO misses and billing spikes.
- A concise UI export and a CSV report for finance and solutions teams.

Out of scope for MVP: automated commit purchases, per-tenant pricing recommendations, and multi-region packing optimizer (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Suggestor returns top 3 commitment profiles for a given tenant within 30s for 90% of queries.
Simulator can replay one week of tenant traffic (up to 10k tenants) in < 2 hours on a single dedicated staging cluster.
Generated profile has estimated monthly delta vs current usage and an estimated 99th-percentile throughput SLO breach probability.
Exportable report with recommended autoscale settings, expected cost, and identified risk windows.
Basic unit and integration tests around simulator determinism and policy fidelity are present in repo.
implementation_notes: Data ingestion: use the existing usage-archive pipeline to pull anonymized tenant traces into the analysis bucket; sample heavy tenants to limit compute cost.
Simulator: implement event-driven playback with configurable worker parallelism; reuse current autoscaler decision logic to ensure fidelity.
Metrics: surface per-simulation traces for token utilization, queue length, provisioned GPUs, and SLO breach events to a temporary Prometheus job and Grafana dashboard.
Cost model: use simplified per-GPU hour cost + estimated egress and infra overhead; make cost inputs configurable per-customer for accuracy.
Scaling policy knobs: evaluation window, cooldown, min/max pool size, burst capacity throttle. Default policy should align with Dedicated team's recommended guardrails.
decision_log: 2026-02-18: Chose to focus on throughput-based fitment (tokens/sec) instead of pure slot-count; tokens/sec maps more directly to customer SLAs.
2026-02-22: Opted to reuse autoscaler implementation for policy evaluation rather than re-implementing decision rules to avoid drift.

2026-03-05: Sampling strategy agreed: deterministic heavy-tenant sampling + 1% random sample across remaining tenants to preserve tail behavior without excessive compute.
